headline: 11 dead as rain-triggered landslides hit Cox's Bazar over two days
summary: A woman was killed in the latest incident in Dariyanagar, bringing the total death toll to 11 across the district, including children and Rohingya refugees.
details: A woman was killed in a landslide in Dariyanagar, Cox's Bazar Sadar upazila, today. The incident occurred around 1:00 pm when a hillside collapsed onto a house, trapping a couple inside.

The couple, Nasima Akter and her husband Jasim Uddin, were rescued by locals. However, Nasima was declared dead upon arrival at Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital, while Jasim is undergoing treatment for serious injuries.
This latest fatality brings the total death toll from rain-triggered landslides in the district to 11 over the past two days.

On Monday, at least nine people, including eight Rohingyas, were killed in separate landslides. Eight of these deaths occurred in different Rohingya camps in Ukhiya upazila, and one person died in Cox's Bazar municipality.
A seven-year-old boy, Md Minhaz Uddin, was killed on Monday evening in the Pekua upazila area of Toitong union, when a wall collapsed on him.
According to the Cox's Bazar Meteorological Office, the district has experienced heavy to very heavy rainfall over several days, weakening hill slopes.
Assistant Meteorologist Abdul Hannan stated that settlements on cut hills, houses built on unstable slopes, and persistent heavy rain have contributed to the casualties.
The district recorded 176mm of rainfall between Monday morning and Tuesday afternoon.

headline_marked: Uttara Bank [[official dies after sharp weapon attack]] in Brahmanbaria
headline: Uttara Bank official dies after sharp weapon attack in Brahmanbaria
summary: Md Ariful Islam, a principal officer, succumbed to his injuries in a Dhaka hospital a day after being attacked in Kasba upazila.
details: Md Ariful Islam, 45, a principal officer of Uttara Bank PLC's Gopinathpur branch, died at a hospital in Dhaka today. He succumbed to his injuries a day after being critically injured in a sharp weapon attack in Brahmanbaria.

The attack occurred around 6:45 PM on Monday in front of Green Health Hospital at Gopinathpur Bazar. A furniture trader named Ali Hossain, 48, allegedly struck Ariful on the head and neck with a sharp weapon before fleeing the scene.
Local residents and colleagues rushed the victim to the Kasba Upazila Health Complex, where he was later transferred to a hospital in the capital for advanced treatment.
According to Kasba Police Station Officer-in-Charge Ali Mohammad Rashed, the attack was allegedly triggered by an argument over a loan disbursement involving the bank branch.
The suspect, Ali Hossain, a resident of Noamura village, is currently at large. Police are conducting raids to arrest him and legal proceedings are underway.
